sampling_model.design: An independent sample \(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) is drawn from the selected multinomial law \(q\); an optional COPAG confidence set is produced from the same sample by a coverage-valid discovery procedure.
sampling_model.units: Each sampled unit is one retained clinical visit with finite coded variables \(V\); the population SCM also contains the binary selection variable \(S\).
sampling_model.treatment: The causal query is the hard intervention \(do(B=b)\); the intervention is hypothetical and sampling randomness comes from the selected observational sample.
sampling_model.overlap: Every selected cell is positive under \(q\). The common lower bound \(\delta\) on population and post-intervention selection is a calibrated sensitivity restriction, not a standard overlap label; the conditional estimand itself only requires \(d_M>0\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(q\) by a simultaneous multinomial confidence region and propagate graph uncertainty by union over a COPAG confidence set; no faithfulness assumption is imposed on the identification class.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 1 and Theorem 1 use finite disturbance-response models and polynomial optimization for a fixed canonical DAG; the graph-permitted NPSEM class does not require every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.

The PAG-compatible optimization concerns faithful no-selection SCMs; its edge semantics are generally incomparable with exact actual-parent semantics under positive but potentially unfaithful selection.
Theorem 4.13 identifies marginal DAG models with the same latent projection and Proposition 7.3 commutes intervention with projection, without proving closure of an exact actual-parent stratum.
Proposition 2 gives sourcewise finite-cardinality reduction preserving observed network behavior, not strict essential-source incidences.

Selected-marginalized directed graphs characterize normalized selected interventional indistinguishability, without retaining the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities calibrated here.

Theorem 4.15 supplies a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm and calculus on specified model classes; the paper distinguishes \(\mathcal M(G)\) from the positive discrete class \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), whose positivity conditions are not implied by positivity of the selected observed law \(q\).
Theorem 5 gives nonemptiness, openness, and density of faithful distributions in its total-variation Markov model, not an equal-moment legal lift on an unfaithful exact-graph boundary.
Criterion inversion yields consistent set estimators, rates, and confidence regions for identified sets defined by population minimizers.
Width-adaptive endpoint intervals attain uniform asymptotic coverage for an interval-identified scalar as identification width approaches zero.
Resampling and screening followed by a union of graph-specific intervals gives asymptotic coverage for a fixed causal effect after causal discovery.

body.tldr: This note studies bounded finite graph-legal response fibers for selection COPAGs without claiming that the full positive, potentially unfaithful arbitrary-SCM fiber is closed.  One saturated superarchitecture per topological order gives at most \(N!\) architecture branches before dense table enumeration; exact essential-feature signs determine the actual selected MAG, and singly exponential one-block real-algebraic procedures return algebraic endpoint witnesses or certificates excluding all bounded compiler branches.  Universal legal lifting and full-fiber closure remain open.  Independently, the graph-free selected-law and two-margin premises imply an explicit finite-state envelope whose endpoints are attained in the complete all-circle one-source subclass and therefore in every permitted family containing those witnesses.  The binary interval \([1/20,39/40]\) is an audit instance, and confidence-fiber inference provides finite-sample outer coverage for the survivor-selected cardiac-surgery use case of Lee et al.

project_justification.gap: Chen and Mooij give a sound-and-complete COPAG identification algorithm on specified model classes; Yang et al. optimize over faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; Duarte et al. optimize a fixed canonical DAG; and Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models. None settles whether the exact actual-parent COPAG fiber for a positive, potentially unfaithful selected law is closed or has attained endpoints. This note also leaves that general question open, while formalizing it and proving bounded-finite and saturated special-case results.
project_justification.niche: The tractable object constructed here is the bounded finite graph-legal response fiber, a finite union of semialgebraic strata. Its essential-feature signs determine the exact selected MAG, and real-algebraic procedures decide whether a boundary value of this bounded image has a legal representative or is excluded from all bounded branches. Equality with, and closure or attainment of, the full arbitrary-SCM fiber remain exactly oeq:universal-legal-lifting.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies an invariant essential-feature index and exact polynomial legality test, one saturated superarchitecture for each topological order, and singly exponential existential-semialgebraic endpoint certificates for the bounded finite image.  It proves a graph-free finite-state outer envelope, one-source endpoint attainment for the complete all-circle COPAG, and the resulting sandwich transfer to every permitted family containing those witnesses.  It designates the compelled-collider case as the first unresolved kill test for universal legal lifting and retains finite-sample confidence-fiber coverage without asserting endpoint convergence for the full arbitrary-SCM fiber.

body.related_work: Richardson and Spirtes define maximal ancestral graphs under latent marginalization and selection conditioning.  Evans canonicalizes latent DAG margins and makes latent projection commute with intervention, but these model-equivalence results do not close an exact functional-essentiality stratum.  Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give sourcewise cardinality reduction preserving network behavior, not strict source-incidence witnesses.  Duarte et al. fix a canonical DAG and optimize graph-permitted finite-disturbance NPSEMs without requiring every displayed edge to remain functionally essential.  Yang et al. treat faithful no-selection PAG-compatible SCMs; that faithful edge semantics is generally incomparable with the actual-parent semantics used here under potentially unfaithful selection.  Carey et al. characterize normalized selected-marginalized models, which do not retain the absolute natural and interventional selection probabilities calibrated by the two margins.  Chen and Mooij are closest: they give a sound-and-complete identification algorithm and calculus, while distinguishing \(\mathcal M(G)\) from \(\mathcal M_d^+(\mathcal P)\); positivity of the selected observed law \(q\) is not equated here with every positivity condition defining their positive discrete class.  Boeken, Forré, and Mooij establish openness and density of faithful laws, which does not produce an equal-moment lift on an unfaithful boundary.  Basu supplies the critical-point sign-sampling and one-block quantifier-elimination results used for the bounded compiler's certificates and complexity.  Chernozhukov, Hong, and Tamer, Imbens and Manski, and Chang, Guo, and Malinsky inform confidence-set inversion; the formal inference claim here remains finite-sample outer coverage.  Lee et al. are the clinical consumer: their FCI and LV-IDA analysis conditions on discharge alive and acknowledges both selection bias and graph ambiguity.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A positive exclusive-or support-deletion family can hold the selected law and intervention moments fixed while an actual shared-source incidence vanishes, so ordinary moment compression does not preserve exact graph legality.  Saturated superarchitectures remove redundant subset enumeration but do not repair this topological obstruction.  A negative algebraic certificate excludes every bounded finite compiler branch at the tested value; absent universal legal lifting, it cannot exclude an equal-moment repair in the arbitrary-SCM superclass.
body.honest_scope: The proved scope comprises source merging by realized child set, sourcewise moment preservation on a fixed permitted architecture, saturated ordered superarchitecture embedding, exact polynomial legality for bounded finite response models, singly exponential one-block endpoint decisions for the bounded image, the transferable saturated envelope, and finite-sample confidence-set event inclusion.  Equality between arbitrary selected SCMs and the bounded compiler, preservation of exact graph legality under general source compression, and closure or attainment of the full positive unfaithful fiber remain open.  No faithfulness, density, minimum edge strength, or positivity of every essential-feature polynomial is added.  In particular, positivity of selected \(q\) is not treated as the stronger positivity defining another paper's model class, and a bounded-branch non-lift is not a superclass impossibility result.
